surviving.title: ERROR-voids-the-run is required, but under early stopping 'rerun after ERROR' is itself a selection mechanism, and per-pair retry is biased whenever the error depends on the agent
surviving.claim: CONTRACT.md is right that an errored pair in the consumed prefix must make the run ERROR (dropping it or scoring it 0 changes E[d]). What it and PLAN.md leave unstated is what happens next. With early stopping, a run's chance of finishing without a harness error falls with its length, so rerunning after ERROR until one run completes over-selects runs that stopped early with a decisive verdict; this happens even when errors are independent of arm and outcome, and it does not happen in v1's fixed-N design. Retrying the errored pair instead avoids that effect only if the error is independent of the agent's behaviour, which v1 semantics do not give: a raising or timed-out check function and infra exit code 75 are all ERROR.
surviving.recommendation: Confirm in ADR 0011 that an ERROR inside the consumed prefix can never be dropped or scored 0, and pre-register one of these policies. (1) Keep ERROR-voids-the-run: state that the guarantee covers the first run only, treat a rerun after ERROR as a new campaign, and have the runner put the errored run's id into prior_runs itself rather than rely on the author. (2) Preferred if live model APIs are in scope: no void and no retry, worst-case scoring per direction as in (c), plus a pre-registered cap on errored trials above which the run is ERROR. Each test stays valid by the same theorem because the scored difference is pointwise below (PASS test) or above (BLOCK test) any resolution of the errored trials; the spike did not calibrate this, so it needs its own enumeration or simulation before adoption. (3) A retry of the same pair is legitimate only for a pre-registered class of faults raised before the agent under test has executed any step (so it cannot depend on agent behaviour), with a bounded attempt count and every attempt stored. It is never legitimate for grader_error, timeouts or infra exit codes, and v2.0 should ship without it.

surviving.recommendation: Specify both derivations as hashes and freeze them with golden vectors run in CI on 3.11 to 3.14, Ubuntu and macOS. Cell for pair i: for attempt a = 0, 1, ...: h = SHA-256(b"arci-suite/1 cell" + 32-byte schedule key + i as 8 bytes big-endian + a as 4 bytes big-endian); v = first 8 bytes of h as a big-endian integer; accept when v < 2^64 - (2^64 mod N) and return v mod N, with cells indexed in canonical sorted order. The rejection step almost never fires but makes the draw exactly uniform. This also gives random access by pair index, which the gate and a batch runner both want, and can be re-derived in any language. Trial seed for pair i: the same construction with tag b"arci-suite/1 seed", reduced to a non-negative integer below 2^53, shared by both arms of the pair (keeps v1's pairing) and a function of the pair index only. Do not make the seed a function of the cell alone: every repetition of that cell then replays the same scenario and, for the model-free fixture, returns the identical difference, so the gate would be testing a mean over N frozen scenarios instead of the cells' success probabilities. Do not key it on a per-cell occurrence counter either, since the conditional mean of d would then depend on past draws. If random.Random is kept anyway, use only random() from an integer seed, which is the documented guarantee, and accept that floor(N*random()) is not exactly uniform.

- **Kernel randomness from the seed:** `worker.py:132` passes `spec.seed` to the toolset factory, `worker.py:150` seeds the agent rng with `f"{spec.seed}:agent"`, `toolbox.py:278` and `:322` seed the fault rng, and `demo/world.py:35-37` derives the scenario from the seed. `schedule.py:53` gives v1 a per-pair seed shared by both arms.
- **Python guarantee:** the random module's reproducibility note guarantees only `random()` under a compatible seeder; `randrange` has a documented 3.2 change. This is from my knowledge of the docs, not re-fetched (no network). The docs do not name `choice`, `shuffle` and `sample` individually, so "explicitly allowed to change" is slightly strong for those.
- **Stable in practice:** my own script (3,000 rounds of `randrange` over n in 10, 30, 60, 300; 2,000 `random()` draws; a str-seeded stream) gave identical fingerprints on CPython 3.9.6, 3.11.16, 3.12.13, 3.13.12 and 3.14.7: `2b3521af36899760`, `d02cc585c74a4207`, `a46da93936dec9df`. The reviewer's exact fingerprints are not reproducible without their script, but the conclusion is.
